parsed.reason: The "Yes, please" is a bare agreement with empty standingQuestions. The last assistant message said "I'll keep watching and text you when they post." The "Yes" lands squarely on that — the parent is confirming they want Hale to keep watching and notify them. The reply correctly identifies this and confirms that exact thing ("I'll keep checking Cartwheels for the Tiny Gym fall dates and text you as soon as they're posted."). It does not ask a clarifying question, does not present a menu of options, does not send the parent to the app, and does not invent any detail. It is clean, short, and does exactly the job. A minor note: the prior message already said Hale would keep watching, so the reply is essentially a restatement of what was already promised — but that is the correct handling of a bare "yes" that confirms an ongoing action. No blemishes worth docking a point for.
